pure-announcement.rationale: This is a design/reference document about protocol architecture and invariants, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts (mcp-authorization-hardening, attested-per-agent-identity, mcp-stateless-core) address MCP-server authorization and identity, not this gateway's channel-ownership architecture or its client/node protocol split - different mechanism and scope.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims are the project's own design invariants and wire-protocol description, directly checkable against openclaw's own repository.

durability.rationale: The core pattern - one long-lived process owning every channel connection, exposing a typed schema-validated protocol to separate client and node roles, with trust escalating from auto-approved local connects to explicit device pairing off-host - is an architecture decision that outlives the specific port number, event names and library choices (Baileys, grammY) mixed into the same page.

actionability.rationale: A reader designing a similar system gets concrete decisions to copy: give one process sole ownership of each external session, validate every inbound frame against a schema, require idempotency keys on side-effecting calls, and grade trust by connection origin - these are actionable design choices, not a landscape description.

atomicity.rationale: The gateway-ownership-plus-typed-protocol-plus-tiered-trust pattern is one coherent idea statable in a paragraph; the wire-format, codegen and remote-access specifics illustrate that one idea rather than introducing separate unrelated ones.
